development.what: the tuning seeds and the tuning planes: the control of (a) and the three singles of (b) ran here, and the combination was chosen from their held-out scores; every development run of this build (--no-fresh) ran here too

heldOut.what: the held-out seeds and planes (new task draws for both planes, searched and held-out): built after the combination was chosen; the tuning never built, searched or scored them, and no development run touched them

retired.exposedBy: a 3 s smoke run (--wall-s 3 --tune-seeds 2 --arm-seeds 2 --fresh-seeds 2) of an earlier build of bench/plateau.mjs at 2026-09-27T01:30Z
retired.why: those strings were exposed by that smoke run, so no run of this build uses them; the held-out side moved to the heldout namespace

split.withinEveryRun: the held-out draw of a plane is read only to write a row; selection, the restart clock, the hall of fame and which migrant is offered read the searched matrix and the clock alone (test/plateau.test.mjs swaps the held-out draw and gets the identical searched trajectory in every arm)

bar.rule: on the held-out seeds, the chosen combination beats the control's mean final held-out score by more than the seed-to-seed noise (the larger sample sd of the two arms) on BOTH planes, and its mean plateau second is later than the control's on both
bar.control: the same loop with novelty, transfer and restart all off, on the same seeds and the same planes, run in the same batch of worker threads

statement: One organism-year is declared to be one generation of the whole population (64 children) on a plane. Two planes the plain search does not saturate were run for 120 wall seconds per run, one generation of each in turn, with the held-out score read every 0.1 s: the grid plane (tasks/grid.mjs, 6175 components, 4 searched draws of 160 tasks, a length cap of 64, scored on a held-out draw of 160 tasks) and a synthetic cover plane (2048 generated components over 384 task families, 4 searched draws of 256 tasks, a length cap of 48, scored on a fresh draw of 256 tasks), the same shapes on the tuning and the held-out seeds. On 5 tuning seeds the plain control last rose on the held-out score at 12.2 +- 8.0 s on grid and 65.8 +- 37.8 s on synthetic, ending at 122.40 +- 0.89 and 225.00 +- 4.53 (mean +- seed sd). Three interventions each ran beside the control on the first 5 of those seeds: behaviour-keyed archive cells (novelty), descriptor-matched elites crossing between the planes every generation (transfer) and a re-seed from the archive's most distant cells after 12 s without a searched rise (restart). Final held-out on grid: novelty 121.00 against 122.40 (plateau 1.8 s against 12.2 s); transfer 122.20 against 122.40 (plateau 12.3 s against 12.2 s); restart 122.20 against 122.40 (plateau 30.6 s against 12.2 s). On synthetic: novelty 224.40 against 225.00 (plateau 52.4 s against 65.8 s); transfer 224.80 against 225.00 (plateau 70.0 s against 65.8 s); restart 222.20 against 225.00 (plateau 45.8 s against 65.8 s). By a rule fixed before the runs the singles chose transfer (no single was at or above the control on both planes, so the single with the largest summed gain was graded). On 5 held-out seeds, on planes built from task seeds the tuning never touched, transfer ended at 118.00 against the control's 119.20 on grid (noise 3.16, plateau 4.9 s against 26.1 s) and 216.40 against 217.80 on synthetic (noise 7.05, plateau 43.6 s against 37.0 s). The bar (beat the control by more than the seed noise and plateau later, on both planes) is not met. The machine was shared with other builders, so every second is a contended wall-clock second and a re-run moves these numbers (a run is cut by the clock, not by a count of generations); they are the numbers of this run, stamped by its at field. No model was called.

declaration.declaration: one organism-year is one generation of the whole population on a plane, so organism-years equal generations
